actions.name: Control Flow Integrity
actions.description: Enforcing legal control flow transfers during application process execution.
actions.reason: Control Flow Integrity enforces legal control flow transfers, preventing code injection attacks and aligning with secure design principles.

actions.name: Application Configuration Hardening
actions.description: Modifying an application's configuration to reduce its attack surface.
actions.reason: Application Configuration Hardening reduces attack surface by securing configuration settings, a core secure design principle.

actions.name: Secure Coding
actions.description: Establish guidelines to prevent vulnerabilities.
actions.reason: Secure Coding establishes guidelines to prevent vulnerabilities, directly supporting secure design principles in application architecture.

actions.name: Principle of least privilege
actions.description: Implement robust access control mechanisms, enforce the principle of least privilege, and regularly update and patch systems to close security gaps that could be exploited for privilege escalation.
actions.reason: Principle of least privilege enforces minimal access rights, a foundational secure design practice for application architectures.

actions.name: Trusted Library
actions.description: A trusted library is a collection of pre-verified and secure code modules or components that are used within software applications to perform specific functions. These libraries are considered reliable and have been vetted for security vulnerabilities, ensuring they do not introduce risks into the application.
actions.reason: Trusted Library uses pre-verified secure code modules, ensuring components adhere to secure design principles through vetted dependencies.

actions.name: Vulnerability Scanning
actions.description:
Vulnerability scanning is used to find potentially exploitable software vulnerabilities to remediate them.
File formats such as pickle files that are commonly used to store machine learning models can contain exploits that allow for arbitrary code execution. Both model artifacts and downstream products produced by models should be scanned for known vulnerabilities.
actions.reason: Vulnerability Scanning detects existing vulnerabilities in software assets for remediation.

actions.name: Code Signing
actions.description: Enforce binary and application integrity with digital signature verification to prevent untrusted code from executing. Adversaries can embed malicious code in ML software, models and Library. Enforcement of code signing can prevent the compromise of the machine learning supply chain and prevent execution of malicious code.
actions.reason: Code Signing ensures software integrity, preventing tampering that could introduce new vulnerabilities.

actions.name: Network Vulnerability Assessment

actions.reason: Network Vulnerability Assessment enables root cause analysis by examining vulnerabilities in network design and interdependencies, revealing systemic risks rather than isolated node issues.
